rows.anchor: they come to believe that they have gained "mastery over nature", with no conceivable limits to what they may yet achieve

rows.speaker: author

rows.anchor: denotes the suddenness and unexpectedness with which doom is bound to encompass the evildoers

rows.anchor: Ibn Kathir points out that it is addressed to all believers, and that it refers to their behaviour towards everyone

rows.anchor: Be humble before God and do not behave with false pride towards anyone

rows.anchor: they were the King's cup-bearer and baker, both of them imprisoned for unspecified offences
